news.title: Paraguay coach Gustavo Alfaro wants team to play for beleaguered nation when they face S’pore, Japan
news.lede: With Paraguay facing challenging times back home, Gustavo Alfaro said his team are looking to lift the country’s spirits with their performances against Singapore and Japan. SINGAPORE – Living up to his moniker ‘El Professor’, Paraguay coach Gustavo Alfaro did not disappoint with his philosophical answers in his pre-match press conference on Nov 12. The 64-year-old Argentinian, who is known for referencing the likes of Einstein and Aristotle in his media interviews, was in his element when asked what advice he would give to Singapore’s 36-year-old rookie international coach Gavin Lee. “I started coaching at 30, and obviously, the world of football is a very big question mark with permanent quests for answers,” said Alfaro with a genial smile, ahead of the opening match of the Mizuho Blue Challenge between his side and the Lions at the National Stadium on Nov 13.

news.title: United States withdraw from U-17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears-Reports
news.lede: The United States have withdrawn from the upcoming FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar because of security concerns linked to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, according to reports from American media. The decision was communicated to players just over a week before the tournament is scheduled to begin on 19 November, with US Soccer Collective and The Athletic reporting that the country's withdrawal was linked to the deteriorating security situation in the region. The development raises further concerns about the impact of the conflict on international sporting events, with several competitions across the Middle East having already been cancelled, relocated or rescheduled.

news.title: USA pull out of U17 World Cup in Qatar over safety concerns
news.lede: The USA have withdrawn from the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, which begins in just over a week, citing the risk of conflict in the region. A letter sent to players from the US Soccer Federation explaining the decision referred to the US state department’s travel advisory for Qatar. It issued a level three travel advisory last month, a day after Yemen’s Houthi rebels carried out deadly airstrikes on Riyadh’s international airport, warning Americans not to travel to Qatar due to the “risk of armed conflict” and the “potential [for hostilities] to escalate beyond” areas which had already been attacked. US Soccer’s letter to players reads: “Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances … we are no longer able to participate in the tournament.

news.title: England: Harry Kane targets European Championships, World Cup and Champions League to add biggest team prizes to Ballon d'Or
news.lede: Harry Kane will become England's record appearance maker on Thursday night - but the Ballon d'Or winner now has his sights set on the biggest team trophies in football. England captain Kane will win his 126th cap for his country against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley. The landmark moment comes just weeks after he was crowned the best player in the world. But while the striker has ended his long wait for team glory with back-to-back Bundesliga titles at Bayern Munich, as well as a German Cup, he is now eager to kick on again and land the most prestigious prizes for club and country.

news.title: Under-17 World Cup: USA withdraw from Qatar tournament over safety concerns
news.lede: The USA reached the last 32 of last year's Under-17 World Cup, the first of five successive editions to be held annually in Qatar. The USA have withdrawn from the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar because of the risk of armed conflict. In a letter sent to players and seen by news agency Reuters, US Soccer said it made the decision "in light of current circumstances". It cited advice from the US Department of State, which issued a level three travel advisory, external for Qatar last month.
